task: Add an opt-in Granite gateway adapter and validate the shape of each Granite rubric stage before checkpointing.
nonGoals: No frontend or public contract edits, production rollout or provider change, allowance ceiling or CPU changes, live inference in CI, or unrelated service changes.

outcomes.description: The opt-in Granite adapter uses the default gateway, explicit generation settings, bounded response parsing, and guarded neuron reservation and settlement.
outcomes.evidence: Adapter regressions cover request shape, malformed responses, evidence shape, usage settlement, and denial before fetch.

outcomes.description: Validate each Granite stage envelope before it can contribute to scoring or be recorded as a completed checkpoint.
outcomes.evidence: Frozen stage examples cover all rubric stages and known malformed inspection and category regressions.

outcomes.description: Exercise one bounded end-to-end audit from submission through stored report with isolated storage and deterministic provider fixtures when live allowance cannot be verified.
outcomes.evidence: Record submission, prepared artifact, provider wire capture, report score, evidence and metered usage.

process.description: Commit the plan before implementation, preserve source-bound evidence and obtain independent review.
process.evidence: Git history, eval output, handoff and independent review.

styleEfficiency.description: Keep provider differences at a clear backend boundary, reuse existing admission and evidence validation, and leave UI and production untouched.

exitTest.reason: Provider and stage validation changes preserve the checkpoint storage, ownership and continuation protocol. Deterministic replay and end-to-end coverage verify resumption with matching inputs.

context: Begin from deployed PR #57. Granite is selected explicitly outside production and does not replace the default configured Terra provider. The existing browser-build suite discovers the prepared Granite tests. This replaces an unpublished draft plan with unsupported direct Node commands; the draft branch remains local.
